summary: Cornucopia codes are a family of quantum low-density parity-check codes achieving encoding rates exceeding $1/2$ while maintaining pseudo-thresholds above $0.4\%$ under circuit-level noise, designed for efficient implementation on reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays through co-optimized code geometry and atom-rearrangement protocols. A single $[[2844, 1426, 18]]$ code block encodes 1426 logical qubits with extrapolated logical error rates of $2.6 \times 10^{-16}$ per logical qubit per cycle at physical error rate $0.1\%$, achieving greater than tenfold reduction in qubit overhead compared to bivariate bicycle codes.
motivation: Existing quantum error correction codes face fundamental trade-offs between encoding efficiency, error threshold, and hardware feasibility; reducing physical-qubit overhead without sacrificing fault tolerance is critical for scaling quantum computers.
method: Cornucopia codes employ a block-convolutional construction with affine-permutation-based structure on a quasi-cyclic geometry $\mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_q$, organizing 12 data blocks (six $L$-type and six $R$-type) and six check blocks, with syndrome extraction via 12 layers of transversal CNOTs that compile into simple parallel atom rearrangements (collective cyclic shifts and row permutations) compatible with acousto-optic deflectors.
result: At $p = 10^{-3}$ physical error rate, the $[[2844, 1426, 18]]$ code achieves logical error rate $2.6 \times 10^{-16}$ per logical qubit per cycle using 4266 physical qubits, compared to 68,000+ qubits required by bivariate bicycle codes for equivalent performance; qubit-routing time per syndrome cycle is merely 16.18 ms, three orders of magnitude shorter than demonstrated neutral-atom coherence times of $\sim 10$ s.
